newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 9.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 9. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto turned 76 on Sunday but celebrations were low-key.

The executive board of the government-backed faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) has decided that chairman Surjadi and secretary-general Buttu Hutapea do not need to resign after the party's massive loss of votes at last month's general election.

Indonesia's state-owned plane maker Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN) will send the first prototype of its homegrown N-250 commuter aircraft as well as its CN-235 Maritime Patrol Aircraft to the Paris Air Show this month.
Indonesia's growing consumer demand is expected to boost advertising spending to almost five trillion rupiah ($2.05 billion) this year, up 20 percent from 1996, advertising industry executives said.

The government-recognised faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) has maintained its threat to reject last month's general election results and asked branches not to sign final poll results until the executive board makes a final decision.
The finance department and Bank Indonesia, according the paper's sources, are planning to merge seven state banks into four institutions to allow them to better face the free trade era.
President Suharto has said in a speech in commemoration of senior citizens day, marked this year on his 76th birthday, that old age makes people wiser.
